summary: Evaluate engine-weight-induced bending and thin-walled closed-section torsion at two sections of an idealized tapered cantilever wing box.
textbookChapters: Thin-walled tubes having closed cross sections

problemStatement:
A large under-wing turbofan engine applies its weight to the wing through the pylon. For a simplified Strength of Materials analysis, one wing is modeled as a tapered cantilever wing box fixed at the fuselage. The engine/pylon assembly is represented by a concentrated mass at its center of mass, located a spanwise distance Le from the root and a chordwise eccentricity e from the idealized wing-box shear/reference axis. The same engine weight therefore produces bending and torsion in the inboard wing.

This problem isolates the static engine-weight contribution. The published GEnx-1B dry mass supplies context for me; the wing-box dimensions, engine station, eccentricity, and equivalent wall thickness are instructor-assigned teaching values and are not proprietary or measured aircraft geometry.
engineeringGoal: Determine the engine weight, internal bending moment and torque, tapered section geometry, hollow-section second moment of area, maximum bending normal stress, and thin-walled closed-section torsional shear stress at the root and at x = Le/2. Compare the two sections and state a bounded engineering assessment of this engine-weight-only model.
